title: bn254-pairing-inversion: gated two-level tag-walk rho (121-instruction step), output (P0,[x]Q0), expected work

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, the algorithm in proof.md returns P=P0 in G1 and Q=[x]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z (for z=1: (P0, infinity)); it recovers x with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (the reference run of proof.md section 5, an opened run with the walk cap kept and the run-level caps removed, finds x after at most 107/100 times sqrt(pi r m/(2(m-1))) walk steps in expectation, m=6), H2 (averaged over runs, the elements evaluated for the first time fall in the distinguished set and in the uncertified tag sets at most a stated factor more often than the sizes of those sets) and H3 (at most 2^98 evaluations of already visited elements in expectation), supported by a proved tag lemma, algebra on the pinned constants and toy runs of the scalar recovery (toy store: a hash map keyed by the whole element; production: an ordered red-black tree keyed by the whole element; the toy does not compute the G2 output). Before any other work the algorithm reads one fresh 64-bit coin u and opens the run only when u < K, K = 7229537559736918267, the least integer for which the opened share of runs times the supported success of an opened run reaches 0.39; a closed run costs 64 instructions and is counted as a failure. An opened run finds x by a sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho walk in GT with 6 multipliers g^c z^d: the next multiplier is read from one stored coordinate of the current element, a step computes a 64-bit tag as the inner product of 60 stored 51-bit digits with 60 table words, refines it with a second inner product when it is too close to a boundary, and uses a tag only when it certifies the exact selector (proof.md section 2), the table holds every product of at most 1,250 multipliers, one Fp12 product re-bases the element every 1,250 steps, uncertified elements are evaluated exactly, distinguished elements (90 bits) go to an ordered store keyed by the whole element, and g^x=z is checked before Q=[x]Q0 is computed by Jacobian double-and-add on the G2 twist (at most 2,845,386 counted instructions over all x < r; with the on-twist check charged 4,096 and encoding 4,026, at most 2,853,508, charged 2^22 in addition to the full parent output and fixed row of 2^16 + 2^32) and (P0,Q) is output, which satisfies e(P0,Q)=g^x=z by bilinearity; it continues until it finds x or a counter reaches its cap. The score is an expectation: the expected total computation over the same uniform challenges and fresh coins is at most 2^118.863948 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000). It is not a bound on every run: on every run the total computation is at most 2^129.347893 equivalents, enforced by counters (a trip budget of 1,251 per call of the step loop, a 3-word exit counter compared with its cap at every exit, 2^50 walk starts, 2^50 reports, 16 recoveries). Prices are executed instruction counts of generated AArch64 programs: 121 instructions per walk step, 178 more for a second-level tag, and 15,135 per exit from the step loop (one Fp12 product of 13,843 with the label additions, digits and counters, plus a stated allowance). Both totals include the gate, all input checks, constants, the table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), walk starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^62.877284 bytes in one address space with 64-bit pointers; preprocessing is at most 2^57.970905 equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, the walk's step loop on real windows, the re-base with its counters on both sides of both caps, both tag levels, both sides of both certificate thresholds, the trip budget) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check both tag lemmas and the certified-selector corollary on production-size values; recompute every ledger integer, the gate constant K (and that K - 1 fails), the expected and every-run totals and the score; run the complete algorithm of proof.md to its output in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only. Mode all (and mode output) also runs g2out.check: the pairing output Q=[x]Q0 by counted Jacobian double-and-add on the G2 twist against an independent affine reference on edge and random scalars, Q0 and outputs on the twist and of order r, and the output charge.
